### policy_self_consistency (this task only)

Charter-global conclusions are **cited, not restated**: `_difficulty.md`
§ `policy_conflict_scan`, § `rule_compute_equivalence`, § `action_binding_and_uuids`,
§ `prerequisite_graph`, § `prerequisite_sentences`, § `override_declarations`, § `factor_ladders`.
Findings bearing on this task: **F-D1, F-D3, F-D8**, plus OBS-D5.

**Handling time.** Four writes. The three prerequisite charges are each evaluated on
`initial_state` alone (none of the three reads a binding another writes — the late charge counts
`charge_code='late_fee'` rows, the exit charge and the standby charge count `management_fee` rows and
service requests, and none reads `receivable_balance_usd`), and the closing settlement is evaluated on
`initial_state` + all three real effects. Verified by recomputing each of the three on the opening
world and again after the other two: the figures are identical, so the three are genuinely parallel
and the order among them is immaterial to every scored value.

**No real-world waits.** Every input is an authoritative row already in `initial_state` (the contract,
32 `cafe_ledger` rows, 8 `cafe_service_requests` rows, the market agreement and 16 `market_ledger`
rows) or the synchronous effect of a preceding write of this task. The termination notice was given on
2025-10-20 and already stands on the contract; nothing waits on clearing, approval or a date
advancing. The payment is made by the customer on the call, by ACH, out of the operating account.
Base eligibility holds: `cafe_invoice_payment_terms`' inherited "A late charge is only raised while the
contract stands in mobilizing, active, suspended or in_transition_out, and never on a closed contract"
is satisfied by `status` = in_transition_out, and `cafe_termination_terms`' inherited notice-period
sentence is satisfied (notice 2025-10-20 + 120 days = 2026-02-17, and the approved
`termination_notice` request asks for 2026-04-19).

### problem_chain

Root: the customer asks to **settle the cafe account in full today** →
`cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment` (`trigger: on_request`, subject `cafe_invoice_payment_posted`,
`target_tool` `settle_contract_balance_f9be2425`, **owner = user**).

Its rule carries **three** prerequisite sentences, and nothing else about any dependency:

1. "The closing settlement is fixed only after the late charge owed on the contract's overdue invoice
   stands on its ledger."
2. "Before the closing settlement is worked out, the early exit charge due on the contract ending
   ahead of its term must stand recorded against the contract."
3. "The closing settlement is not worked out until the standby charge owed for the months the cafe has
   stood suspended stands on the contract's ledger."

**Judged against the raw DB at `frozen_time`:**

| # | state required | in the seed | unmet? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | a `late_fee` row for the overdue invoice | `late_fee` rows **do** stand: 2025-07-22 (1,180.00, period 2025-05) and 2025-11-25 (940.00, period 2025-10). The currently overdue invoice is INV-CF-484012, `management_fee` 18,096.00 posted 2026-02-08, unpaid; no `late_fee` names it. | only under the narrow reading |
| 2 | an `early_termination_fee` row | **none anywhere** on the 32-row ledger | **cleanly unmet** ✔ |
| 3 | a `standby_fee` row for the months the cafe stood suspended | `standby_fee` rows stand for 2025-06 and 2025-07 (the first pause, 2025-06-02→2025-07-01); the **second** pause (approved 2025-08-05, effective 2025-08-16, resumed 2025-09-28) carries none | only under the narrow reading |

Edges 1 and 3 turn on a reading the `condition` does not fix (see F-D3 in `_difficulty.md`). Edge 2 is
unambiguous, so the tree does hold, but two of its three announcements are weaker than the `condition`
they carry.

**Nodes, edges, kinds, topological order.** Three prerequisite problems, all `value_input` on the gate
`unsettled_balance_usd`, all resolved before the root: {`cafe_ext_late_charge_assessment`,
`cafe_ext_early_exit_charge`, `cafe_ext_standby_charge_assessment`} → `cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment`.
n = 3, floor max(n−1,1) = 2 `value_input` edges; all three are `value_input`. No cycle.

**Per-edge load-bearing run** (each recomputed by deleting that write's row and its effect on
`receivable_balance_usd`, then re-evaluating the settlement):

| edge skipped | settlement | vs 150,431.90 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| late charge (678.08) | **149,753.82** | moves |
| early exit charge (55,283.28) | **95,148.62** | moves |
| standby charge (26,058.24) | **124,373.66** | moves |

All three bear weight. Note against **OBS-D5**: the 7→4 edge's `effect` claims the count rising "also
moves the equipment deposit returned"; with three charges posted the count is 3 and with the late
charge skipped it is 2, and `equipment_deposit_return_band`'s tier 1 ("two or more") is selected
either way, so on this world the deposit returned stays at 27,200.00. The claim is false here.

**Parallel edges — terminal-state argument.** The three writes do affect one another's *reading*
surface (each raises `receivable_balance_usd` and each adds a `cafe_penalty_fee_posted` row that
`penalty_charges_3m` counts), so the ordering question is real and must be settled. It is settled:
`unsettled_balance_usd` is a **sum**, `penalty_charges_3m` is a **count**, and no one of the three
charges reads any quantity another writes. Every order of the three therefore gives the same three
charge amounts, the same receivable (182,439.60) and the same count (3), so the same terminal state.
**No two orders give two defensible outcomes.**

**No-wait argument.** Each resolving action is one synchronous call —
`post_late_charge_719c9a63`, `post_early_exit_charge_dadd74c6`, `post_standby_charge_21704194` — and
the root is the customer's own `settle_contract_balance_f9be2425`, which she performs on the call.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** All four function bodies in `task_tools.py` are
`ctx.find` → arithmetic on the argument → `ctx.update` → `ctx.create` → return. No branch, no raise,
no status check, no hint.

**Customer's own write.** The root itself is `owner="user"`, and the persona hands it over passively:
*"When the payment is handed to her to make, she makes it, and if she is asked she reads back the
confirmation it gives her."* She also fixes the tender herself ("by ACH rather than by cheque or
card"). ✔ satisfied.

**Isomorphism.** The tree an independent reader derives — three charges to post before the settlement
can be worked out, each announced by a sentence of the settlement policy's own rule — matches the
declared shape, with the reservation recorded above about edges 1 and 3.

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse.** Act now, all four writes. The contract stands `in_transition_out`, written
notice stands from 2025-10-20, and the customer asks for the account to be settled today.

**Object.** `cafe_contracts/a4441acb…` (CS-136) — the only cafe contract the client has ever held, as
she says. Reached via `find_customers` (phone 2015097642 / account code CA-11507) →
`find_cafe_contracts(customer_id=…)`.

**Authorisation and boundary.** She authorises the desk to read, derive and post the charges
("you tell me the number, I'll move the money"), and reserves the payment itself: "she will not hand
over the payment to anyone else… she will make it herself, out of the operating account, and that it
goes by ACH". That is exactly one customer-owned write and three agent writes, and she asks for
nothing further.

**Write 4 — `settle_contract_balance_f9be2425` (owner = user), `settlement_amount_usd` = 150,431.90,
`payment_channel` = "ach".** Evaluated after the three charges, so
`receivable_balance_usd` = 100,420.00 + 678.08 + 55,283.28 + 26,058.24 = **182,439.60**:

| binding | value |
| --- | --- |
| unsettled_balance_usd | **182,439.60** |
| service_gap_days = DAYS(2024-05-06, 2024-08-19) = 105 > 60 → tier 1 | contract_year_elapsed_months = 18 mod 12 = **6** |
| penalty_charges_3m = 3 ≥ 2 and a notice day stands | deposit_returned_usd = RND(68,000.00 × 40/100, 2) = **27,200.00** |
| funding_lots_12m = 2 (2025-06-11, 2025-12-09) ≥ 2 and drawn 69.20 < funded 45,500.00 | subsidy_refund_usd = 45,500.00 − 69.20 = **45,430.80** |
| months_in_service = 18, 12 ≤ 18 < 24, notice stands | inventory_recovery_usd = RND(19,500.00 × 50/100, 2) = **9,750.00** |
| market active; kiosk subsidy funded over 12 months = 18,000.00 + 14,500.00 = 32,500.00 ≥ 26,000.00 | carry_over_pct = **75.00** → refunded after carry-over **11,357.70** |
| suspended days ytd 74 ≥ 10 and notice stands | smallwares_share_pct = **50.00** |
| smallwares_credit_usd | as `compute` has it: RND(12,800.00 × 50/100 × (12 − 6)/12, 2) = **3,200.00** |
| result | MX(0, RND(182,439.60 + 9,750.00 − 27,200.00 − 11,357.70 − 3,200.00, 2)) = **150,431.90** |

*Contrasting reading (F-D1).* The **only** sentence the charter offers on the smallwares credit — and
the verbatim `compute_basis` entry for `smallwares_credit_usd` — is "…**half** the smallwares allowance
printed against the service model is credited back **for each whole month of the contract year still
to run**…". Six whole months still run, so a reader following the rule computes
12,800.00 × 50 % × 6 = **38,400.00**, and the settlement becomes
MX(0, RND(182,439.60 + 9,750.00 − 27,200.00 − 11,357.70 − 38,400.00, 2)) = **115,231.90**. No sentence
anywhere in the rule, in `baseline.rule` or in `compute_basis` licenses the trailing `/ 12` that
`compute` applies. Two defensible answers, **35,200.00 apart**.

**Terminal state.** Four new `cafe_ledger` rows (late_fee, early_termination_fee, standby_fee,
invoice_payment); `receivable_balance_usd` 182,439.60 − 150,431.90 = **32,007.70**.

**Service-period arguments.** `service_period` is a scored, fixed-format argument on all four tools,
and for three of them the policy does not fix it: the standby charge covers a pause spanning **2025-08
and 2025-09** (two months of pause, one posting), the late charge's clock is anchored on a service
credit of 2025-12-25 while the overdue invoice is 2026-02, and the exit charge relates to a closure
dated 2026-04-19. Nothing in the rules or the persona picks one calendar month for any of the three.
Recorded under `findings` as OBS-1.

**Context closure.** All reachable: `find_cafe_contracts`, `find_cafe_ledger`,
`find_cafe_service_requests`, `find_market_agreements`, `find_market_ledger`, `find_customers` +
`verify_caller_identity` on details the persona holds (phone 2015097642, account code CA-11507, zip
02139, profile opened 2021-02-16). Nothing needed is seed-only.

**Computation 4 — closing settlement, gold 150,431.90, whole-baseline 47,026.00.**

| factor | effect | tier taken / rows | baseline | under baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| contract_year_anchor | method | tier 1: service gap 105 > 60 days | `term_months % 12` (declared) | **152,565.23** |
| equipment_deposit_return_band | parameter | tier 1: 3 `cafe_penalty_fee_posted` rows in 3 months, notice day stands | `RND(P('equipment_deposit_usd') × K('whole_deposit_pct')/100, 2)` | **109,631.90** |
| drawable_funding_refund_basis | method | tier 1: 2 funding lots in 12 months, drawn 69.20 < funded 45,500.00 | `F('subsidy_pool_balance_usd')` = 67,413.60 | **144,936.20** |
| opening_inventory_recovery_band | parameter | tier 2: 18 service months, notice day stands | `RND(P('opening_inventory_usd') × K('no_inventory_recovery_pct')/100, 2)` = 0.00 | **140,681.90** |
| outlet_carry_over_band | parameter (**cross_difficulty: market**) | tier 1: market active, kiosk subsidy 32,500.00 ≥ 26,000.00 | `K('no_carry_over_pct')` | **116,358.80** |
| smallwares_credit_band | parameter | tier 1: 74 suspended days ≥ 10, notice day stands | `K('no_smallwares_share_pct')` | **153,631.90** |

All six bear weight and the whole baseline gives 47,026.00, definite and different from gold.
**Two baseline defects bite here:**

- **F-D8 — `contract_year_anchor`'s baseline is dishonest.** The policy's `baseline.rule` says "The
  contract year elapsed is the whole months between the first day of the contract term and the day the
  settlement is worked out" — that is `term_months` = **22**, unreduced, and it is also exactly the
  ladder's fall-through tier ("…the contract year elapsed is the whole months between the first day of
  the term and the day the settlement is worked out"). The factor's declared `baseline` is instead
  `term_months % 12` = **10**. Computing from `baseline.rule` alone gives
  smallwares credit = 12,800.00 × 50 % × (12 − 22)/12 = **−5,333.33** — a **negative** credit, because
  "the whole months of the contract year still to run" comes out at **−10**. So the baseline as
  declared is not the rule's, and the rule read alone is not self-sufficient: settlement **152,565.23**
  under the declared baseline, **158,965.23** under `baseline.rule`, against 150,431.90 under the
  ladder.
- **F-D1** (above, in `task_independent_derivation`) applies to the same binding from the ladder side.

**Near-miss** for this computation: the `subsidy_funding` lot of **2025-02-24** (22,000.00) sits one
month outside the twelve-month window, so `funding_lots_12m` is 2 and not 3 — counting it would move
both the lot count and the funded total. The `market_ledger` `subsidy_funding` rows are both inside the
window, and the earlier `monthly_settlement` rows are excluded from this factor by the `charge_code`
filter the rule names ("the subsidy the client has funded at the market kiosk").

**Counts against the bounds.** 4 / 4 / 5 / 6 factors, each within 4–6; parameter and method counts per
computation (2/2, 3/1, 3/2, 4/2) all clear 2 `parameter` and 1 `method`. Over the task's computations:
**multi-source** present (e.g. `grace_days_band` conjoins a `cafe_ledger` twelve-month count with
`cafe_contracts.termination_notice_date`; `equipment_deposit_return_band` conjoins a ledger count with
the same contract field), and **cross-difficulty** present twice
(`continuing_outlet_allowance` and `outlet_carry_over_band`, both category `market`, both with rows
seeded). No tier anywhere is read off a field that names its own outcome.

## findings

**1 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (also SOURCE-TASK) — the closing settlement's smallwares credit is twelve
times smaller in `compute` than in the rule** (charter-global finding **F-D1**,
`_difficulty.md § rule_compute_equivalence`).
- *Symptom*: the scored settlement can be derived at 150,431.90 or at 115,231.90 from the same charter.
- *Root cause*: the only sentence the charter offers, quoted verbatim as
  `compute_basis.smallwares_credit_usd`, is "…half the smallwares allowance printed against the service
  model is credited back **for each whole month of the contract year still to run**…". `compute`
  implements `RND(P('smallwares_allowance_usd') * smallwares_share_pct / 100 *
  (12 - contract_year_elapsed_months) / 12, 2)`. "For each whole month" is a multiplication; the
  trailing `/ 12` appears in no sentence of the `rule`, of `baseline.rule` or of `compute_basis`.
- *Evidence*: `cafe.extended.yaml` → `cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment.rule` (final sentence),
  `compute` binding `smallwares_credit_usd`, `compute_basis.smallwares_credit_usd`, and the
  `smallwares_credit_band` ladder, whose tier 1 reads "half the smallwares allowance printed against
  the service model".
- *Demonstrated consequence*: on this world `smallwares_allowance_usd` = 12,800.00,
  `smallwares_share_pct` = 50.00 and `contract_year_elapsed_months` = 6, so six whole months still run.
  The rule gives 12,800.00 × 50 % × 6 = **38,400.00**; `compute` gives **3,200.00**. The settlement is
  MX(0, RND(182,439.60 + 9,750.00 − 27,200.00 − 11,357.70 − **38,400.00**, 2)) = **115,231.90** against
  gold **150,431.90** — **35,200.00** apart, on the one figure the customer is asked to pay.
- *Affected artifact*: `cafe.extended.yaml` → `cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment`; `tasks/1.json` →
  `evaluation_criteria` final `call_user_discoverable_tool` argument `settlement_amount_usd` and
  `computations[3].expected`.
- *Relation to previous revisions*: first audit of this difficulty; no prior revision.

**2 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED — `contract_year_anchor` declares a baseline its own `baseline.rule` does not
state, and that rule read alone gives a negative number of months** (charter-global finding **F-D8**,
`_difficulty.md § factor_ladders`).
- *Symptom*: the baseline a reader of the computation document would apply is not the baseline the
  factor declares, and neither is the ladder's fall-through.
- *Root cause*: `baseline.rule` says "The contract year elapsed is the whole months between the first
  day of the contract term and the day the settlement is worked out" — `term_months`, unreduced — and
  the ladder's fall-through tier repeats that wording. The declared
  `baseline: contract_year_elapsed_months: term_months % 12` reduces it by whole years, which no
  sentence of the charter states.
- *Evidence*: `cafe.extended.yaml` → `cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment.baseline.rule` (third
  sentence), `factors[0].baseline`, `factors[0].ladder[2].method`, and `compute` binding
  `contract_year_elapsed_months`.
- *Demonstrated consequence*: on this world `term_months` = MONTHS(2024-05-06, 2026-03-10) = **22**.
  Under the declared baseline (22 mod 12 = 10) the settlement is **152,565.23**; under `baseline.rule`
  as written (22) "the whole months of the contract year still to run" is 12 − 22 = **−10**, the
  smallwares credit is **−5,333.33** and the settlement is **158,965.23**; the ladder gives
  **150,431.90**. Three figures from one policy, and the one an unaided reader of the baseline reaches
  is a *negative credit* — so the baseline is not self-sufficient in the sense the standard requires.
- *Affected artifact*: `cafe.extended.yaml` → `cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment.baseline.rule` and
  `factors[0]`; `tasks/1.json` → `computations[3].factor_sensitivity[0].baseline_result` = 152565.23,
  which is the declared baseline's figure and inherits the same defect.

**3 — observation (from charter-global F-D3) — two of the three edge `condition`s do not identify the
row they require, and rows of the named charge_code already stand at the opening.**
- The late-charge edge requires "a cafe_ledger row of charge_code `late_fee` stands against the
  contract for **the overdue invoice**, and `cafe_contracts.receivable_balance_usd` carries it". Two
  `late_fee` rows stand at the opening (`2025-07-22`, 1,180.00, period 2025-05; `2025-11-25`, 940.00,
  period 2025-10) and the receivable carries both. The standby edge requires "a cafe_ledger row of
  charge_code `standby_fee` stands against the contract **for the suspended months**"; two `standby_fee`
  rows stand (2025-06-30 and 2025-07-31) for the first of the two pauses.
- GT's `why_false` for each silently narrows to the right row ("nothing answers the invoicing that has
  run unpaid since"; "the pause that ran from 2025-08-16 to 2025-09-28 carries no standby charge"), but
  the narrowing is in the proof field, not in the `condition` or in the prerequisite sentence the agent
  reads. Graded as an observation because the third edge (no `early_termination_fee` row anywhere) is
  cleanly unmet, so the tree still holds and the consequence is not demonstrable here.

**4 — observation (from charter-global OBS-D5) — the late-charge edge's `effect` is false on this
world.** It asserts "…the contractual charges counted in the three month window rise by one, **which
also moves the equipment deposit returned**". With all three charges posted `penalty_charges_3m` = 3;
skipping the late charge leaves 2; `equipment_deposit_return_band`'s tier 1 condition is "**two or
more** contractual charges", so the deposit returned is 27,200.00 either way. Recomputed: the skipped
run gives 149,753.82, differing from 150,431.90 by exactly 678.08 — the charge itself, with no deposit
movement.

**5 — observation (OBS-1) — `service_period` is a scored argument on all four writes with no policy
derivation.** The standby charge covers a pause spanning 2025-08 and 2025-09; the late charge's clock
is anchored on a service credit of 2025-12-25 while the invoice that has run unpaid is 2026-02; the
exit charge relates to a closure dated 2026-04-19. GT records "2026-03" — the month of the call — on
all four. That is the most natural default given each tool dates its own posting today, but no sentence
of the charter says so, and the tool docstrings only say "the billing period the … charge is recorded
against".

**6 — observation (OBS-2) — the late charge's whole baseline is 0.00.** Substituting all four
baselines gives `grace_days_allowed` = 10, `days_overdue` = DAYS(2026-02-08, 2026-03-10) = 30, and
`months_charged` = MX(0, int(20/30)) = 0, so the baseline figure is **0.00**. It is definite and
different from gold, which is what the standard asks; but `post_late_charge_719c9a63`'s contract states
the amount "must be a positive amount", so a reader of the baseline alone concludes that no late charge
is due rather than arriving at a wrong figure.

**7 — observation (OBS-3) — two tiers of `standby_fee_base_band` coincide on this world.** Tier 1
("the management fee most recently invoiced") and tier 2 ("the mean of the management fees invoiced
over those three months") both give 18,096.00, because the only two invoices in the window
(2026-01-08 and 2026-02-08) are equal. The tiers are distinct as stated, so this is not a ladder
defect; it does mean the scored figure cannot distinguish a reader who took tier 1 from one who took
tier 2.

**8 — observation — the seeded `market_ledger` is consistent with the market charter.** Checked
because the sibling task's pantry seed is not (`_difficulty.md § F-D9`): "Standard Micro Market" prints
`management_fee_basis: subsidy_true_up`, `monthly_sales_guarantee_usd: 7800.00` and
`subsidy_funding_minimum_usd: 4200.00`, against seeded monthly settlements of 7,600.00 and subsidy lots
of 18,000.00 and 14,500.00. No contradiction found.

settled together with task 0's F-R1, since the two are the same defect and a standard applied to one and
not the other is no standard. The factor bears weight either way (baseline 58,812.00 against gold
55,283.28), so no scored value is at stake.

against `charge/100 × weeks`. It has been repaired by the same standard as task 0's

other is no standard. On this world:

## new_defects (this task)

**OBS-R3 — observation — the rounding-point move on `notice_relief_usd` introduced an unlicensed
intermediate rounding, latent on this world.** The brief asked whether "same on this world" is the same
as "same"; it is not, and the direction matters:

| | expression | rounding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rounds 1–2 | `RND(exit_charge_before_allowances_usd / 50 * int(…/7), 2)` | once, at the end |
| round 3 | `RND(exit_charge_before_allowances_usd / 50, 2) * int(…/7)` | per week, then multiplied |

On this world the two agree exactly, because 90,480.00 ÷ 50 = **1,809.60** is already exact to the cent
— which is why the exit charge is still 55,283.28 and why no scored value moved. They diverge wherever
the per-week amount is not exact: at an exit charge of 1,000.55 over 7 whole weeks, rounding first gives
140.07 and rounding at the end gives 140.08. The intent behind the move is reasonable — the prose
"reduced by one fiftieth of itself **for each of them**" does read as a per-unit amount taken a number
of times — but `cafe_ext_early_exit_charge`'s only rounding sentence is on the result ("the result is
rounded to the nearest cent and is never less than nil"), so the per-week rounding is not stated
anywhere, and the move traded a form the rule did state for one it does not. Recorded as an observation,
not a red light, because no consequence is demonstrable on this world; it is the same question as task
0's F-R2 and should be settled with it, in whichever direction.

**OBS-R4 — observation — one of this task's ladder fall-through faces is worded differently from its
rule.** `outlet_carry_over_band` T2 reads "the nil carry-over share", while
`cafe_ext_closing_settlement_payment`'s rule states that outcome as "none of that funding is carried
over to another outlet"; the phrase "nil carry-over share" appears nowhere in the rule or in
`baseline.rule`. The charter's own convention elsewhere is for the fall-through face to name the nil
constant and for the rule to use that name — `smallwares_credit_band` T2 says "the smallwares share is
nil" and the rule says "the smallwares share is nil". Both readings mean the same thing and both select
0.0, so no second answer follows and this is not a red light; but the ladder is what the KB renders, so
it is one of the two faces of that family my sweep found still open (the other is in
`cafe_ext_standby_charge_assessment`, which also serves this task — see `_difficulty.md` § `revision_3`
→ OBS-R4).

**F-R3 did not bear on this task**, and I re-checked that rather than assuming it. Applying the
criterion to this task's four policies — stripping every `RND` whose own sentence names no rounding —
reproduces gold in all four: **678.08**, **55,283.28**, **26,058.24**, **150,431.90**. In round 4 nine

**The two changed computes, checked against their new prose in exact decimal.**

| | new sentence | literal reading | gold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| late charge | "The late charge is the amount still outstanding taken at the late charge rate, **rounded to the nearest cent**, charged for each month charged, and held to the late charge ceiling printed against the service model." | 42,380.00 × 1.6 % = **678.08** struck to the cent; charged for each of 1 month = 678.08; under the 4,800.00 ceiling | **678.08** ✔ |
| standby charge | "The standby charge is the standby fee base taken at the standby rate, **rounded to the nearest cent**, charged for each month of pause charged, and the late resumption loading is then applied once to the figure that step leaves; the result is rounded to the nearest cent." | 18,096.00 × 60 % = **10,857.60** struck; charged for each of 2 months = 21,715.20; loading applied once = **26,058.24** | **26,058.24** ✔ |

Both sentences now describe a per-unit price struck once and charged as many times as the unit occurs,
which is what `RND(x, 2) * n` does; under the criterion these are correctly on the per-unit side, since
neither months charged nor months of pause is a count against a fixed whole. Neither change moves a
figure here, for reasons I checked rather than assumed: `months_charged` is **1**, so striking before or
after multiplying cannot differ; and the standby's per-month figure **10,857.60** is already exact to
the cent.
